correctness.rationale: In W=1 the norm resultant eliminating b between b³=V and U=(b+1)³ is the proposed plane cubic; (b+1)³ is not invariant under b→ζb over k(b³), so its minimal polynomial has degree three. The product-ratio map on the projective torus splits: in x6=1 choose x2,x4,x5 freely and solve for x1,x3. Thus the cubic pulls back to an irreducible torus hypersurface; no coordinate divides the sextic, and the finite cubing image has dimension four. In the nonzero-product locus the chain rule reduces singularity to (-1:1:1), whose Hessian has determinant 243. If exactly one product is zero the other two satisfy the indicated linear relation and the base derivative in the missing-product direction is a unit, so both variables of that pair must vanish; exactly two zero products are impossible, and all three zero products lie on Y and give zero gradient. The two defining quadrics of Y meet in a smooth torus translate on the torus; its affine boundary has dimension at most three, strictly below the minimum dimension four of a component. The codimension-two complete intersection is thus generically reduced and unmixed, hence integral and of degree four projectively. Each remaining component is a nondegenerate quadric surface not contained in Y. The split torus map gives the ordinary double crossing at the generic point of Y (the quadratic form splits over k and hence over k(Y)); the boundary charts give xy times a unit plus or minus t³, yielding the stated A2 germs. R1 fails at Y. On the dense torus, a scaling outside the stabilizer imposes a second independent linear condition on the three products, hence does not contribute to generic fibers. The two independent scaling constraints give |G|=27 and Q/G is normal, finite and birational over X. Independently recomputed a resultant, the nodal quadratic form and all three unit terms symbolically.
residual_risks: Characteristic zero throughout. The calculation does not resolve the nonreduced singular scheme or analyze the germs at stratum intersections.

value.rationale: This fully identifies where and how normality is lost in the next coordinate power of a standard Grassmannian, as distinct from its normal square. The three separately described A2 surfaces and the one split crossing divisor distinguish singularities on the boundary and on the torus. This is an exact geometric classification, not just an equation/degree calculation or a check on a finite set of points.
residual_risks: No family theorem for other powers and no description of a conductor, intersections or global normalization singularities is asserted.
